Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //ww,v.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 117 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 DIR. WINSTON L. PLAZA Civil Service Commission Caraga Regional Office Doongan Road, Butuan City 8600 Dear Dir. Plaza: This pertains to your letter dated 29 June 2022 addressed to Dir. Lilibeth A. Famacion of DILG Regional Office XIII on whether or not the Department prescribes the qse of CSC Form No. 7 Revised 2018 (Clearance Form) for outgoing Local Chief Executives. It concerns the person who has the authority to sign the certification of outgoing Mayors/Governors and Vice MayorsNice Governors clearing them of work-related, möney, and property accountabilities and certifying that the elective officials have no pending administrative case from their respective agency. It is respectfully advised that with respect to the issuance to local elective officials of Certificate of No Pending Case before this Department, the Trial and Investigation Division (TID, Legal and Legislative Liaison Service (LLLS) processes and issues the same with the Service Director as the signatory. Being an ISO enrolled process of the TID, LLLS the certificate is currently issued in accordance with the format approved in said ISO enrolled process following the approved procedure thereon. No processing of clearance is required prior to the issuance of this Certificate of No Pending Case as the same merely entails verification Of TID's database on pending cases. Hence, we submit that the use of Clearance Form No. 7 Revised 2018 is not applicable to this process. Going further, it was mentioned in your letter that CSC Form No. 7 Revised 2018 (Clearance Form) is required for appointive officials in case of their promotion, reappointment, or transfer involving movement from one department/agency to another and reemployment. However, the follow-up query is about the clearanæs or certifications of outgoing elective officials for them to be cleared from work-related, money and property accountabilities and to certify that they have no pending administrative case. We are of a position that accomplishment of the same may not be necessary for outgoing Local Chief Executives (LCEs) who are elective officials. Given the nature of the responsibility of Local Chief Executives as head of Local Government Units, their respective accountabilities are subject to post-audit by the Commission on Audit (COA), while their criminal, civil and administrative liabilities committed during their tenure of office attach to them even after turnover of. local governance. Thus, they may not be cleared of accountabilities by mere accomplishment of clearance form to be signed by the head of offices which have "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

been under their supervision as Local Chief Executives. Finally, the prevailing Department issuances on Local Governance Transition do not specify that the subject clearance form should be complied with by outgoing Local Chief Executives. The rationale being the accountability or non-accountability as well as pendency of cases against these officials should not in any way hinder smooth transition of local governance which has the paramount importance. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
